title: Basic accessibility web features
body:
### Checklist

- [X] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [X] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

To begin with, it is a great product. In its current state, it seems advisable to generate a final web page with considerations for web accessibility. This includes aspects such as the page name, language, structure, and named links. Currently, these tags cannot be controlled and may result in errors or warnings in accessible web page verification tools.

### Why?

The product is described as excellent. However, it lacks certain features related to web accessibility. Enhancing web accessibility can improve user experience and ensure compliance with accessibility standards. This proactive approach can also prevent errors and warnings in verification tools.

### How?

To address this, efforts should be made to generate a final web page that incorporates aspects of web accessibility. This may involve adjusting tags related to page name, language, structure, and links to comply with accessibility guidelines. By implementing these changes, errors and warnings in verification tools can be minimized, thereby improving the overall accessibility and usability of the web page.

### Additional Context

I know there are some questions in forums about compatibility e.g. with 508 standards (https://discuss.streamlit.io/t/508-compliance-for-streamlit/13579) which of course would be great but my recommendation would be to start with simple compatibilities that do not incorporate too much development overhead, or diminish Stremlit's capabilities.

Thanks so much to everyone who reported and pushed on accessibility initiatives here 🎉 
This issue collected several distinct concerns over time, so we're triaging them against recent work and more focused trackers:

| Concern | Status | Tracking / notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Controllable page name / title | Done | Supported via `st.set_page_config(page_title=...)` |
| Unlabeled sidebar collapse / expand buttons | Done | #17170 |
| Unlabeled main menu (⋯) button + ARIA on wrong element | Done | #13878 — `aria-label`, `aria-haspopup`, and `aria-expanded` are on the menu button |
| Named links | Partial | Empty-label `st.page_link` / icon-only chrome naming in #17170. Heading anchors: #13329 (fixed in #13378). Meaningful link text for app content remains author-owned (WCAG 2.4.4). |
| Page structure (landmarks, headings, skip links) | Partial | Shell landmarks / skip link still need focused work — tracked in #17416. Wiki inventories leave WCAG 2.4.1 unscored. |
| Controllable HTML language (`lang`) | Open | Tracked in #15726 |
| Broader Section 508 / WCAG compliance | N/A (framework) | Streamlit is a framework, not a finished app, so it can't be blanket "508 compliant" — conformance depends on each deployed app (author content, charts, custom components, etc.). We'll keep improving shell/widget accessibility and the APIs authors need so apps *can* meet WCAG / 508 criteria. Track concrete gaps via `area:accessibility` issues and the wiki inventories (`accessibility-wcag.md`, `accessibility-theme.md`). |

We're closing this issue so new accessibility reports land in focused tickets instead of piling up here. The specific UI bugs from this thread (sidebar controls, main menu) are fixed; anything still open is linked in the table above. If you hit a new gap, please open a dedicated issue with the `area:accessibility` label.
